record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: Let P_α(z) = e^{2πiα} z + z^2, where α is an irrational real Bruno number, and let S_α be the maximal connected open neighborhood of 0 on which P_α is analytically linearizable. Does there exist a Bruno number α such that the boundary ∂S_α of this Siegel singular disk is a smooth C^∞ embedded circle in the complex plane?

evidence.quote: 1. Does there exist α1 a Bruno number such that ∂Sα1 (the boundary of Sα1 ) is a C∞ submanifold of C (a circle) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an irrational real number $\alpha$, consider the quadratic polynomial
$$P_\alpha(z) = e^{2\pi i \alpha} z + z^2.$$
The Bruno series of $\alpha$ is defined by $B(\alpha) = \sum_{n \ge 0} \frac{\log q_{n+1}}{q_n}$, where $p_n/q_n$ are the convergents of the continued fraction expansion of $\alpha$; the number $\alpha$ is called a Bruno number if $B(\alpha) < \infty$. By a theorem of Bruno and Yoccoz, $\alpha$ is a Bruno number if and only if $P_\alpha$ is analytically linearizable near $0$, i.e., there is a holomorphic injection $\varphi$ from a neighborhood of $0$ in $\mathbb{C}$ to $\mathbb{C}$ with $\varphi(0)=0$, $\varphi'(0)=1$, and $\varphi^{-1} \circ P_\alpha \circ \varphi(z) = e^{2\pi i \alpha} z$. Let $S_\alpha$ denote the maximal such linearization domain (the Siegel disk of $P_\alpha$ around $0$).

Question: Does there exist a Bruno number $\alpha$ such that the boundary $\partial S_\alpha \subset \mathbb{C}$ is a $C^\infty$ embedded circle (i.e., a $C^\infty$ submanifold of $\mathbb{C}$ diffeomorphic to $S^1$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been solved affirmatively. Avila, Buff, and Chéritat ("Siegel disks with smooth boundaries", Acta Mathematica 193 (2004), 1–30) proved the existence of a (dense uncountable) set of irrational numbers $\alpha$ (necessarily Bruno, since linearization requires the Bruno condition by Yoccoz) such that $P_\alpha$ has a Siegel disk with $C^\infty$ smooth boundary; a result of this kind had earlier been announced by Pérez-Marco (1993).

status_evidence.title: Siegel disks with smooth boundaries (Avila–Buff–Chéritat)
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a dense uncountable set of angles α such that every quadratic-like map with a fixed point of multiplier e^{2πiα} has a Siegel disk with C^∞ boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of α (Bruno) for which the quadratic Siegel disk boundary is C^∞ smooth is established.

status_evidence.title: Siegel disks/Quadratic Siegel disks - Scholarpedia
status_evidence.snippet: The existence of α with quadratic polynomial having a Siegel disk with C^∞-smooth boundary was first announced by Pérez-Marco in 1993 and proved by Avila–Buff–Chéritat.
